thread:
alex: Heads up — after last night's GPU scale we saw ~10% of headless services in eu-west return stale endpoints for pods that moved nodes. CoreDNS SRV records looked OK but kube-proxy conntrack had mappings to drained node IPs.

rita: Oof. Any error logs? service discovery or endpointslice controller lag?

sam: I saw endpoint-slice controller CPU spike in the metrics around 02:10 UTC. Might be delayed slice reconciliation.

infra-bot: Alert: EndpointSliceControllerRestarted eu-west-1 at 2026-03-17T02:12:07Z

maria: Another suspicion: NAT session affinity from the edge load balancer kept SNAT mappings to old node IPs. If backend pods moved, traffic still got sticky to drained nodes until conntrack expired.

alex: Repro steps I ran:
```bash
kubectl get endpointslices -n inference -l kubernetes.io/service-name=infer-api -o wide
kubectl describe svc infer-api -n inference
kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep infer-api
``` 
Found EndpointSlices listing pods that no longer existed on that node.

rita: Can you check kube-proxy mode? iptables conntrack TTLs can be long. If we're on iptables + conntrack, sticky NAT can persist longer. ipvs has different semantics.

sam: Checked — kube-proxy is in iptables mode for eu-west. We had recent kubelet/node restarts during GPU scale. conntrack table filled briefly.

maria: Short-term fix: drain-evict gracefully (no immediate node deletion) and bump sessionAffinity timeout on the Service:
```yaml
service.spec.sessionAffinity: "ClientIP"
service.spec.sessionAffinityConfig.clientIP.timeoutSeconds: 60
```
That reduces stickiness. Also consider setting externalTrafficPolicy: Local if appropriate.

alex: Agreed. Long-term we should test switching kube-proxy to ipvs and tune endpointslice resync. Also add a pre-drain hook to flush conntrack on node scale-down.

rita: I'll open a runbook PR with the drain hook and a playbook to force endpointslice reconcile (`kubectl rollout restart deployment endpointslice-controller -n kube-system`) — test in staging first. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment triggered: runbook/endpoint-fix -> staging at 2026-03-17T15:03Z

sam: Cost note — keeping nodes around longer costs money but frequent node churn is more expensive in tokens and incidents. We need a middle ground.

alex: Yup. Let's sync tomorrow and run a staged kube-proxy ipvs trial in eu-west staging.

rita: filing ticket: #INFRA-8124 — "eu-west headless endpoints stale after GPU scale: session-affinity/conntrack"
